definition: Efficacy is how well a treatment works in producing its intended benefit. In this context, it refers to how effective an added medicine is when combined with another treatment for depressive disorder.

reasons: The packet does not provide a dictionary-style or explicit definition of the term “efficacy”; it only uses the word “efficacy” in the background context of a study (“efficacy and safety… have not been systematically evaluated”).
The definition’s first sentence (“how well a treatment works in producing its intended benefit”) is a general definitional claim not supported by the supplied packet text.

The second sentence narrows efficacy to “an added medicine… combined with another treatment for depressive disorder”; while the packet mentions adjunctive addition of Chinese patent medicines to SSRIs for depressive disorder, it does not define efficacy in those terms.
The packet uses the word 'efficacy' in a study context but does not define it as 'how well a treatment works in producing its intended benefit.'

The packet only supports a specific research question about the efficacy of adding Chinese patent medicines to SSRIs for depressive disorder; it does not support the broader explanatory definition or the claim that this is what efficacy means.
The wording 'in this context' is acceptable only as a topic context, but the definition still overstates the source by turning a study objective into a dictionary definition.
